nodes.summary: Let $m, A, B \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $d, e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $d(q) < 4$ and $e(q) < 4$ for every $q < m$. Then $A \cdot 4^m + \sum_{q < m} d(q) \, 4^q = B \cdot 4^m + \sum_{q < m} e(q) \, 4^q$ holds if and only if $A = B$ and $d(q) = e(q)$ for every $q < m$.

For a list $b$ of pair bits, a vertex $v$ and an index $q$, the test is true when bit $b_q$ is set and $v$ is one of the two entries of $p_q$. An index past the end of $b$ counts as an unset bit, and for $q \ge m$ the pair $p_q$ is taken to be $(0, 0)$.
